problem_structure: [S] Q1 derives a two-beam SiC thickness model with refraction and dispersion.
[S] Q2 preprocesses two-angle spectra, performs joint inversion, and systematically evaluates reliability.
[S] Q3 derives multi-beam conditions, detects their presence, solves the Si data with an Airy model, and tests whether SiC needs the same complexity.

question_to_model_mapping.Q1: Snell and Fresnel equations, Cauchy dispersion, FFT initialization, nonlinear least squares.
question_to_model_mapping.Q2: Equal-interval resampling, AsLS/Hampel/Savitzky–Golay processing, sliding FFT/SNR band selection, robust two-angle Levenberg–Marquardt fitting, piecewise Cauchy model.
question_to_model_mapping.Q3: Airy multi-beam model, coherence/reflectivity/absorption conditions, FFT detection, joint constrained least squares, and a two-beam sufficiency test for SiC.

model_choice_rationale: [S] Cauchy dispersion captures wavelength dependence without an overly large parameter set.
[S] Joint-angle fitting shares physical thickness and dispersion while allowing angle calibration, reducing single-angle bias.
[S] Airy interference is selected for silicon only after sharp fringes, secondary-frequency evidence, and interface reflectivity indicate appreciable multiple reflection.

claim_evidence_map.assessment: [I] Strongly supported by internal diagnostics and two-angle agreement.

claim_evidence_map.claim: [S] Piecewise Cauchy fitting improves high-wavenumber residuals without materially changing thickness.
claim_evidence_map.evidence: Physical pages 12–14: systematic residual identified, d changes from 7.619 to 7.604 μm, and high-band RMSE falls.
claim_evidence_map.assessment: [I] A well-evidenced negative-to-corrective modeling step.

claim_evidence_map.claim: [S] Silicon exhibits significant multi-beam interference and has thickness about 3.814 μm.
claim_evidence_map.evidence: Physical pages 21–25: fringe-shape, FFT, cross-angle evidence, Airy fit, and residual amplitude below about 0.02.
claim_evidence_map.assessment: [I] Internally well supported.

claim_evidence_map.claim: [S] SiC multi-beam contribution is negligible.

problem_structure: [S] Q1 models fetal Y-chromosome concentration against gestational age and BMI using longitudinal data.
[S] Q2 partitions BMI and jointly chooses group boundaries and NIPT times to minimize failure and delay risk.
[S] Q3 adds age, pregnancy count, and parity to produce individualized timing adjustments.
[S] Q4 constructs a female-fetus chromosome-abnormality screening rule with calibration, multiple-testing control, and repeated-measure consistency.

question_to_model_mapping.Q1: Logit-transformed linear mixed model with quadratic GA/BMI fixed effects and random intercept/slope; GLM comparison.
question_to_model_mapping.Q2: Threshold-attainment probability, monotonic smoothing, failure-plus-time risk, five-segment BMI optimization, and dynamic programming.
question_to_model_mapping.Q3: Extended mixed model with Elastic Net selection, covariate timing shifts, constrained two-stage optimization, and dynamic programming.
question_to_model_mapping.Q4: Male-sample calibration by chromosome/gestational-age strata, robust residual distributions, Z scores, Benjamini–Hochberg q values, threshold search, and repeated-measure aggregation.

model_choice_rationale: [S] Mixed effects address repeated measurements and between-pregnancy heterogeneity.
[S] Dynamic programming enforces ordered, non-overlapping groups while finding a global minimum over discretized BMI.
[S] Elastic Net limits multivariable expansion and the female classifier controls multiplicity and batch effects.

parameter_provenance_quality.evidence: [S] Sample counts and fitted coefficients derive from the supplied clinical data, but failure scaling κ, time-risk coefficients, segmentation penalties, and several screening thresholds are internally chosen or optimized with limited external clinical provenance.
